findings.reason: the section must cite the real owner (serve.py) or extend it, otherwise it forks a fourth git-date reader.
findings.text: §3's premise "read with the git date cache the audit already keeps" is false: reckon/doccheck.py contains zero git references and the audit reads os.path.getmtime directly at line 531, while the git last-commit machinery it describes lives in reckon/serve.py:1432 (_git_last_committed) with its persisted _GIT_LAST_MODIFIED_CACHE at reckon/serve.py:1316; the plan is about to build the lookup it believes it is borrowing

findings.reason: §3 should thread the commit-date source through derived_plan_age so the audit and the roadmap/archive agree, naming reckon/serve.py:1432 as the git lookup to reuse, instead of adding a parallel read.
findings.text: the age owner to extend is derived_plan_age (reckon/doccheck.py:230), which already resolves plan-modified then file-mtime and is consumed by reckon/archive.py:87 and reckon/roadmap.py:945,968, and the audit loop at line 531 bypasses it entirely to read mtime itself; the census of git-date readers is burying this as a fifth: reckon/serve.py:1432 _git_last_committed, reckon/metadata_index.py:681 git_last, reckon/fleet_index.py:33 _commit_days, plus derived_plan_age

findings.reason: the write paths omit the callers the contract change reaches (_store.py, and the second _plan_html.py assignment), so the change would land half-applied and the write-refusal would change without being declared.
findings.text: §2 changes derive_impl_from_sections so an uncovered plan returns a declarations-derived figure instead of None, but names only _plan_html.py in its write paths while the function is consumed at THREE further sites whose behaviour the change silently alters: reckon/_plan_html.py:1125 and reckon/_plan_html.py:2234 (both set impl_source, and both must learn the third value "declarations"), and reckon/_store.py:2606, which refuses authoring impl whenever the call is "not None" and so will start refusing impl writes on partially-recorded plans; reckon/_plan_html.py:1939 is a fourth caller reading the same None-contract

findings.reason: two of the three callers live outside the declared write paths, so the wiring census is incomplete and the roadmap and new-plan refusal would keep reporting plans unwired that §5 declares wired.
findings.text: §5 rewrites unwired_plan_finding to accept section-level relations and gate-evidence, but lists only reckon/doccheck.py, skills/reckon-create/SKILL.md and the test in its write paths while the function is called from THREE sites that build its inputs and must pass the new ones: reckon/doccheck.py:858, reckon/roadmap.py:1287, reckon/mcp_discovery.py:221

findings.reason: the sections add audit/definition surface without accounting for it against the week's 1626 definitions / 23 refusal families, which the rubric holds each adding section to state.
findings.text: §2 adds the enum value "declarations" to IMPL_SOURCE_ENUM (reckon/_schema.py:112) and the audit flag impl-meta-stale; §3 adds AGING; §4 adds SPRINT_MEMBERSHIP (census across s2/s3/s4) — and no section names what it retires or merges, or explains why nothing can be

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no section proposes a new module; §2–§5 each extend one existing function (derive_impl_from_sections, derived_plan_age/audit loop, unwired_plan_finding) behind the interface that already carries the behaviour.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3 would resolve a plan's last-commit date inside the audit rather than extending the age owner derived_plan_age (reckon/doccheck.py:230) and the git last-commit owner _git_last_committed (reckon/serve.py:1432); three git-date mechanisms already coexist.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1626, cli_options 351, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §2, §3 and §4 each add audit-flag surface (impl-meta-stale, AGING, SPRINT_MEMBERSHIP) and §2 adds an enum value, and none of the three sections names what it retires or merges, or states why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 and §4 correctly name the existing owners they extend (derive_impl_from_sections, IMPL_SOURCE_ENUM, project_state.read_resource), but §3 credits the audit with a "git date cache" it does not keep, and §5 changes a function whose other callers it never names.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the sections extend the existing functions in place rather than adding parallel wrappers over them; the one parallel-path risk (§3's git read) is reported under reuse_search and duplicate_owner.
